addendum4.id: Re-Degradation Reveals Resolution | CVPR 2027 | addendum v4 | registered after run 3 and before run 4
addendum4.scope: Frozen v1.0, addenda v2 and v3 and every rule registered so far stay exactly as they are, and the checkpoints of runs 1-3 are reused unchanged. Addendum v4 adds block B12 (the official CIFAR-10-C benchmark with six standard CIFAR-10 classifiers) with rules K1-K4, and four exploratory analyses X1-X4 of checkpoints that already exist (no pass/fail).
motivation: run 3: the plug-ins were tested on ImageNet-C corruptions re-created on our ten datasets with frozen encoders, while label-free accuracy estimation is usually reported on the official CIFAR-10-C files with classifiers trained on CIFAR-10

addendum5.id: Re-Degradation Reveals Resolution | CVPR 2027 | addendum v5 | registered after run 4 (CIFAR-10-C) and before run 5
addendum5.scope: Frozen v1.0 and addenda v2-v4 stay exactly as they are and the checkpoints of runs 1-4 are reused unchanged. Addendum v5 (i) defines the identity-preserving plug-in X@s_hat v5, (ii) adds blocks B13 (CIFAR-100-C), B14 (fMoW: real ground-sample-distance shift, pan-sharpened and multispectral views of the same acquisitions), B15 (the additive-noise semigroup), B16 (CIFAR-10-C with the v5 plug-ins, the identifier ablation and synthetic blur + noise) and B17 (the five real pairs of B4 with the v5 plug-ins), and (iii) registers rules L1-L10 and the reported analyses L11-L13. The contribution is framed as the identified level s_hat: a label-free, physically calibrated blur level that any label-free accuracy estimator can use.
motivation: run 4, P3: the plug-ins were not identities at s_hat = 0. COT@s_hat and AE-LS@s_hat re-calibrate even at zero (UCM->RESISC45 at s_hat = 0, sigma = 0: COT +2.4 and AE-LS +13.5 pp), and the v2 noise path added 3.3 DN of noise where its own model check rejected (PatternNet->RESISC45: ATC +4.9, AE-LS +11.4 pp)
run 4, K1-K4: on CIFAR-10-C the identified level tracks the PSF variance (K3) and COTT@s_hat does no harm (K2); B13 tests both on a second standard benchmark that no earlier run touched

runs 3-4: the real-world evidence covers identification (R4-R6, V1) but not estimation; B14 uses fMoW, whose metadata gives each image's ground sample distance and whose multispectral copy of every acquisition is about four times coarser

run 4, I1/X4: classic metrics identify noise-free blur as well as s_hat; the identifier ablation asks whether the downstream estimate depends on which identifier supplies the level, in particular under noise
the framework is stated for observation semigroups; B15 tests a second one (additive Gaussian noise: re-noising reveals the noise variance)

plugin_v5.level: s5 = the v2 level (s_v11 when v1.0 flags the condition, else s_hat)
plugin_v5.noise: sigma5 = sigma_v11 only when v1.0 flags the condition and the v2 model check accepts (flagged2 = False); otherwise 0
plugin_v5.identity: X@s_hat v5 equals X exactly when s5 = 0 and sigma5 = 0, for ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COT, COTT and AE-LS

forms.ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COTT: calibrated on A2 re-degraded to (s5, sigma5), as in v2 (identities at zero by construction)
forms.COT: delta form: COT + [(c(s5) - e(s5)) - (c(0) - e(0))], c = COT transport cost and e = error of the probe on A2 re-degraded to the level
forms.AE-LS: delta form: AE-LS + beta log(1 + s5), beta = the level coefficient of the AE-LS+s regressor

identifiers.lap: variance of the Laplacian (calibrated, as ATC@NR)

identifier_ablation.noise: level only (sigma = 0) for every identifier, so the four plug-ins differ only in the level
identifier_ablation.conditions: Gaussian-PSF and other-blur corruptions and every synthetic condition in B13 and B16; every condition in B14

cifar100c.data: CIFAR-100-C (Hendrycks and Dietterich, ICLR 2019; Zenodo record 3555552, CIFAR-100-C.tar, md5 11f0ed0f1191edbf9fa23466ae6021d3, CC BY 4.0) and the CIFAR-100 test set (Krizhevsky, 2009, binary version, fine labels)
cifar100c.split: as B12: A2 = clean test images 0-4999 (source calibration); B = test images 5000-9999 (targets); the known-corruption oracles use the corrupted copies of images 0-4999
cifar100c.order_check: the CIFAR-100-C labels must equal the fine test labels in every severity block
cifar100c.model_source: torch.hub chenyaofo/pytorch-cifar-models (BSD-3-Clause; trained on the CIFAR-100 training set; weights from the repository's GitHub releases)
cifar100c.source_grids: as B12 (S_ACC and the meta-set blur range scaled by (32/224)^2)

synthetic_cifar.images: the full B split, re-degraded in floating point by the 32-px DCT heat semigroup plus keyed Gaussian noise (the same noise blocks feed the pixel identification and every classifier)

cifar10c_v5.content: the v5 plug-ins, the identifier ablation and the synthetic blur + noise conditions on CIFAR-10-C; B12 results are not replaced

fmow.data: fMoW-rgb validation split (Christie, Fendley, Wilson and Mukherjee, CVPR 2018), public AWS bucket spacenet-dataset/Hosted-Datasets/fmow/fmow-rgb (no credentials). Every acquisition has a pan-sharpened RGB image (rgb) and a multispectral RGB image (msrgb) about four times coarser; the metadata give each image's ground sample distance (gsd)
fmow.view_filter: cloud_cover <= 20, a visible object box, and the 112-m window fits inside the image
fmow.grid: every image is resampled to 0.5 m per pixel (Pillow bicubic, antialiased when reducing); a 224-px window (112 m) is centred on the first visible object box and shifted to lie inside the image
fmow.split: locations are split by a keyed hash: 40% source and 60% target. A1 and A2 (alternating by keyed hash) take the sharpest rgb view with gsd <= 0.50 m of each source location; the targets are every eligible rgb view of the target locations (at most 4 per location) and the msrgb image of the same acquisitions
fmow.merge: from the finest bin upwards, a bin with fewer than 90 images merges into the next coarser bin (the last bin into the previous one)
fmow.encoders: the six method encoders (frozen) with the linear probe of B11 (trained on A1)

noise_semigroup.statement: additive white Gaussian noise is a semigroup in its variance: adding variance eta to y = x + sigma xi gives variance sigma^2 + eta. The mean power of the orthonormal DCT modes with lambda >= lambda_hi is affine in eta with unit slope. Re-noising the target over an eta grid and fitting the line gives an intercept; its difference to the clean source's intercept identifies sigma^2 (source-relative)
noise_semigroup.blur_scaling_32: levels at 32 px are the 224-px levels times (32/224)^2
noise_semigroup.image_sets: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 test sets (source = images 0-4999, target = 5000-9999) and the fMoW source crops (source = A2, target = A1)
noise_semigroup.comparators: the v2 joint blur + noise fit (sigma_v11), the median-absolute-deviation estimate (Donoho and Johnstone, 1994) on the same DCT band and Immerkaer's (1996) Laplacian-mask estimate; every estimate is source-calibrated (target variance minus source variance)

real_v5.content: the B4 units re-run with the v5 plug-ins (same data, splits, encoders, conditions and random streams)

L2.ci: 95% bootstrap, corruptions resampled first, then their severities (models move together)

L3.test: X@s_hat v5 < X for the 6 plug-in pairs, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells, Holm over the 6 pairs

L4.statistic: Spearman rho between the v2 level and the empirical Gaussian-equivalent PSF variance (as B12)

L5.conditions: synthetic blur + noise with sigma >= 4 DN
L5.test: ATC with the s_hat level has a lower error than ATC with the variance-of-the-Laplacian level and than ATC with the spectral-slope level, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells, each p < 0.01

L6.statistic: Spearman rho between each target condition's v2 level and its median gsd

L7.conditions: target conditions with median gsd >= 0.60 m
L7.test: X@s_hat v5 < X for the 6 plug-in pairs, one-sided Wilcoxon on paired cells (encoder x condition)

L8.statistic: pooled MAE of COTT@s_hat v5 minus COTT over every target condition
L8.ci: 95% bootstrap, gsd bins resampled first, then their conditions (encoders move together)

L9.statistic: median over the 10 keyed target subsets of |sigma_hat^2 - sigma^2| / sigma^2 of the re-noising estimate, without blur, for sigma in {2, 4, 8, 16} DN
L9.pass: every image set and every sigma

L10.test: non-inferiority of X@s_hat v5: upper 95% bound of the pooled paired difference X@s_hat v5 - X <= +1.0 pp (hierarchical bootstrap)

reported.L11: CIFAR-100-C per corruption group: ATC@s_hat v2, COTT@s_hat v5, COT@s_hat v5 and the strongest of the 11 baselines
reported.L12: fMoW: identified level and accuracy per gsd bin; share of the accuracy drop explained by blur (source re-blurred to the identified level), as X2

addendum6.id: Re-Degradation Reveals Resolution | CVPR 2027 | addendum v6 | registered after run 5 and before run 6
addendum6.scope: Frozen v1.0 and addenda v2-v5 stay exactly as they are and the 73 checkpoints of runs 1-5 are reused unchanged. Addendum v6 (i) temperature-scales every label-free estimator and plug-in on the labelled source and reports both versions, (ii) defines a label-free attribution score phi and the phi switch, (iii) replaces the AE-LS adapter by a bias-transfer form and adds MaNo with and without the plug-in, (iv) adds block B18 (ImageNet scale: ImageNetV2 as the labelled source, the ImageNet-C definitions on its other half, and the real ImageNet-C blur archive), block B19 (identification compared with blind kernel estimation by KernelGAN) and blocks B20-B23 (temperature-scaled re-runs of B13, B16, B14 and B17 that also save per-image logits), and (v) registers rules Q1-Q12 and the reported analyses Q13-Q17. The paper's claims are reorganised into six claims (claims map below); every rule of v1.0-v6 stays in the ledger with its verdict.
motivation: run 5: no estimator was temperature-scaled, while ATC (Garg et al., ICLR 2022) and COT (Lu et al., NeurIPS 2023) calibrate every method on source validation data. The CIFAR-100 classifiers are 10.6 pp overconfident on clean A2 and raw COT on CIFAR-100-C has 11.7 pp MAE; the linear probes are 7-15 pp overconfident on the harder datasets

run 5, exploratory and post hoc: phi = (c_src(0) - c_src(s_hat)) / (c_src(0) - c_tgt) tracked the labelled share of the accuracy drop explained by blur (Spearman 0.97 over 21 settings, 0.89 over 1,217 cells), and switching the plug-in off for phi < 0.5 removed the LandCover.ai 25 -> 50 cm harm while keeping the CIFAR blur gains. Both are confirmed here only on data that no run has touched (block B18)
run 5: the v5 AE-LS adapter (AE-LS + beta log(1 + s5)) over-corrected on real targets (shifts of -7.8 pp on LandCover.ai and -8.8 pp on fMoW)

reviewers will expect an ImageNet-scale test, the newest accuracy estimator (MaNo, NeurIPS 2024) and a comparison with blind kernel estimation from cross-scale recurrence (Michaeli and Irani, ICCV 2013; Bell-Kligler, Shocher and Irani, NeurIPS 2019)

temperature_scaling.reference: Guo, Pleiss, Sun and Weinberger, ICML 2017
temperature_scaling.fit: one temperature T per classifier (linear probe or trained head): minimise the mean negative log-likelihood of the clean labelled source calibration split A2 over log T in [log 0.05, log 20] (bounded scalar search, tolerance 1e-4)
temperature_scaling.applies_to: every softmax output of every estimator and plug-in: the source at every level, the meta-sets, every target
temperature_scaling.report: pre-T (T = 1, exactly the v1.0-v5 definitions) and post-T; every Q rule uses post-T unless it says otherwise
temperature_scaling.logits: per-image logits (float16) of the clean source and of every target condition are written to the logits folder next to the outputs (not the resume zip); ImageNet targets keep a keyed subset of 1,000 images per condition

plugin_v6.level: as v5: s5 = the v2 level; sigma5 = sigma_v11 only when v1.0 flags the condition and the v2 model check accepts
plugin_v6.AE-LS: bias transfer: AE-LS@s_hat v6 = AE-LS - [b(s5, sigma5) - b(0, 0)], b = the AE-LS prediction on A2 re-degraded to the level (its meta-features read from that set) minus the probe's accuracy there; unclipped predictions inside, the result clipped to [0, 1]
plugin_v6.MaNo: the same bias transfer with the MaNo accuracy prediction
plugin_v6.identity: X@s_hat v6 = X exactly when s5 = 0 and sigma5 = 0, for ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COT, COTT, AE-LS and MaNo

mano.reference: Xie, Odonnat, Feofanov, Deng, Zhang and An, NeurIPS 2024
mano.score: S = (1/(N K) sum_i sum_k Q_ik^p)^(1/p) with p = 4; Q = softmax(q) when Phi > eta, else the second-order Taylor normalisation (1 + q + q^2/2 minus its row minimum, rows summing to 1); Phi = the mean over images and classes of -log softmax(q) (uniform cross-entropy) on the clean labelled source A2, computed once per classifier and temperature, so that every set of a classifier (meta-sets, source levels, targets) uses the same normalisation (the official code also fixes it once per model); eta = 5
mano.inputs: the classifier's logits on the whole set (temperature-scaled in the post-T version), frozen model in evaluation mode
mano.accuracy: a LinearRegression of accuracy on S over the AutoEval meta-sets, as for NucNorm (the paper reports correlations)

attribution.phi: phi = (c_src(0) - c_src(s5, sigma5)) / (c_src(0) - c_tgt), c = mean maximum softmax probability (post-T); undefined when |c_src(0) - c_tgt| < 0.005
attribution.labelled_share: share = (A_src(0) - A_src(s5, sigma5)) / (A_src(0) - A_tgt), on cells with A_src(0) - A_tgt > 0.02 (evaluation only: it uses target labels)
attribution.switch: X_sw = X@s_hat v6 when phi >= 0.5, else X (also when phi is undefined)

imagenet.source: ImageNetV2 matched-frequency (Recht, Roelofs, Schmidt and Shankar, ICML 2019; 10,000 images, 10 per class; Hugging Face dataset vaishaal/ImageNetV2, file imagenetv2-matched-frequency.tar.gz; label = the folder name, the ImageNet-1k class index)
imagenet.preprocessing: Pillow bilinear resize of the shorter side to 256 and centre crop to 224 (the ImageNet-C preprocessing)
imagenet.split: per class the 10 images ordered by a keyed hash of the file name: the first 5 form A (labelled source, 5,000 images), the other 5 form B (target base, 5,000 images)
imagenet.generated: the nine ImageNet-C families of block B9 (Hendrycks and Dietterich, ICLR 2019) at severities 1-5 applied to B, each image with its own keyed stream, then stored as JPEG quality 85 as the ImageNet-C files were; plus clean B stored as JPEG 85
imagenet.synthetic: B re-degraded in floating point by the heat semigroup: s in {1, 4, 16, 64} px^2 and sigma in {0, 3} DN (keyed noise blocks shared by the pixel stage and every model)
imagenet.real: the ImageNet-C blur archive (Zenodo record 2235448, blur.tar, md5 2d8e81fdd8e07fef67b9334fa635e45c, CC BY 4.0): defocus, glass, motion and zoom blur at severities 1-5; per class the 5 validation images with the smallest keyed hash of the file name (the same 5,000 images in every condition); label = the WordNet folder (sorted wnids = class index). These are ImageNet validation images, a different sample than ImageNetV2, so this target mixes a natural shift with blur

motivation: run 7 (block B18, fresh ImageNet data): the v6 plug-ins lowered the error on 0 of 7 estimators on the generated ImageNet-C blur targets (Q5 FAIL; ATC 2.5 -> 7.1 pp, COTT 2.1 -> 4.4 pp post-T) and the phi switch did not keep a gain (Q8 FAIL), while the same classifiers, images and identified levels gave ATC 6.4 -> 0.55 pp on the floating-point synthetic blur targets

storage_plugin.store: the storage step of the target set, read from its files without labels: 'jpeg' with quality q and chroma subsampling c when the targets are JPEG files (q = the IJG quality whose Pillow quantisation tables equal the files' tables, the nearest one by L1 distance of the luminance table when none is equal; c from the files' sampling factors; the modal (q, c) over the set); 'lossless8' when the targets are 8-bit images without lossy compression; 'float' when they are floating-point arrays (images re-degraded in memory)
storage_plugin.re_degradation: D(x) = decode(JPEG_{q,c}(Q8(T_{s5} x + sigma5 xi))) for 'jpeg', Q8(T_{s5} x + sigma5 xi) for 'lossless8' and T_{s5} x + sigma5 xi for 'float' (the v6 form); Q8 rounds to the nearest integer and clips to [0, 255]; JPEG with Pillow (optimize=True), decoding with Pillow; the noise field xi is the one of the v6 level
storage_plugin.plugins: X@s_hat v7 for ATC, ATC-NE, DoC, COT, COTT (the v5 forms), AE-LS and MaNo (the v6 bias transfer) and PT, with the source re-degraded by D instead of the floating-point re-degradation
storage_plugin.phi_v7: phi_v7 = (c_src(0) - c_src(D)) / (c_src(0) - c_tgt) with c the mean maximum softmax probability (post-T); undefined when |c_src(0) - c_tgt| < 0.005
storage_plugin.labelled_share_v7: share_v7 = (A_src(0) - A_src(D)) / (A_src(0) - A_tgt) on cells with A_src(0) - A_tgt > 0.02 (evaluation only)
storage_plugin.switch_v7: X_sw7 = X@s_hat v7 when phi_v7 >= 0.5, else X; blend X_bl7 = X + clip(phi_v7, 0, 1) (X@s_hat v7 - X) (reported)
storage_plugin.identity: X@s_hat v7 = X and X_sw7 = X exactly when s5 = sigma5 = 0 and the store is 'lossless8' or 'float'; for 'jpeg' targets the source passes through the JPEG step even at s5 = sigma5 = 0 (by design)

floor_sensitivity.definition: FSI = mean over s in {1, 4, 16} px^2 of [gap(s, 3 DN) - gap(s, 0)], gap = mean maximum softmax probability minus accuracy of the classifier on the labelled source A2 re-degraded to s by the exact semigroup, with and without 3 DN white noise (the A2 grids every bank computes), in pp, post-T; pre-T reported
floor_sensitivity.meaning: a classifier with FSI >= 4 pp is floor-sensitive: its confidence on a blurred image depends on the image's high-frequency floor (sensor noise, compression), so a re-degradation without that floor mis-calibrates its confidence-based estimators; it needs no target data and no target label

self_selected_decisions: Self-selected: R0 and R2 test the lemma's exact standardisation (no epsilon); the pipeline's N keeps eps = 1e-6 from frozen v1.0, and its deviation from N o A = N is printed, not asserted.

Self-selected: target-condition noise is a seeded numpy float32 field in 32-image blocks; the same blocks feed the pixel identification and every encoder. Source-side noise (degraded A2, AutoEval meta-sets) comes from a seeded torch generator on the device, one field per batch shared across blur levels.
Self-selected: pixel DCTs use scipy.fft (type II, orthonormal) and a sparse binning matrix, both asserted equal to the v1.0 matrix and bincount reference (<= 1e-9 relative).

Self-selected: knee fits use the SSE-by-expansion form and the v1.1 tail fit is vectorised by valid-level pattern; both are asserted against the v1.0 reference on random curves (>= 98% identical grid indices).

Self-selected: R1 and R10 use the closed form int_0^eta Var_{pi_u}(lambda) du = E_{pi_0}[lambda] - E_{pi_eta}[lambda] (log-partition identity), so they test the identity rather than quadrature error; O_x keeps the frozen 32-point trapezoid.

Self-selected: pooled statistics weight datasets equally (mean of per-dataset means), matching the hierarchical bootstrap that resamples datasets first; the addendum's regime statistics average a dataset's seeds before pooling.

Self-selected: COT and COTT use the A2 label marginal as the source label distribution and solve the C x n transportation problem, asserted equal to the n x n assignment on random cases; the target transport costs are computed once per condition and shared by the baselines and the plug-ins (same random streams, so COT and COTT equal their run-1 definitions).
Self-selected: NucNorm accuracy comes from a LinearRegression of accuracy on the normalised nuclear norm over the AutoEval meta-sets; the ICML 2023 paper reports correlations only.
Self-selected: predictions from regressions and confidence differences (DoC, the AutoEval family, NucNorm, DoC@s_hat, COT@s_hat, AE-LS+s_hat) are clipped to [0, 1]; this can only lower their error.
Self-selected: PT_anchor weights are fitted once per target subset, because the anchor features at s = 256 px^2 do not depend on a condition's blur or noise.
Self-selected: the mechanism screen runs on the 120 target tiles per dataset only; the knee rho uses no source tiles, which would cost about 45 GPU-minutes without entering any rule.

Self-selected: stress tests (noise sweep, PSF misspecification, JPEG) run on a random subsample of at most 240 B images per dataset; the v1.0 check uses the full A2 calibration split, the v2 noise-model check at most 240 A2 images.
Self-selected: images (and LandCover.ai tiles) whose minimum per-channel std is below 0.5 DN are dropped (logged for images), because a constant channel makes the normalised response undefined.
Self-selected: the six method encoders stay in CPU RAM and move to the GPU one at a time, which avoids about 150 reloads while keeping one encoder on the GPU.
Self-selected: in the certificate experiment an abstention counts as a coverage failure, and n_Q = 'all' is a single repetition on the full B.

Self-selected: in MODE=full a failed check_figure triggers tick thinning and a re-check; a remaining problem is logged in the manifest instead of aborting after the GPU blocks. In DRY_RUN the check is strict.
Self-selected: DRY_RUN writes to outputs_dryrun/ and its checkpoints carry a dry-run flag, so a smoke test can never be resumed into a real run.

Self-selected: one universal session budget (REDEG_BUDGET_H, default 11 h, measured from the first cell) replaces the projection-based dropping of run 1, which dropped all seed replication on a warm-up throughput estimate: units run in a fixed order (B2, B3, B4, B5, B6), each unit part (pixel stage, one encoder pass, one mechanism unit) starts only if its live estimate fits before the compute stop (budget minus a 0.25 h packaging reserve), and nothing is dropped; once the budget is used up an IPython input transformer replaces every later cell by a one-line skip notice, except the cells marked @always-run (inventory, completeness, packaging, final cell).

Self-selected: a session acquires only the datasets its pending units read; data-dependent assumption checks of an earlier session are kept when no dataset is loaded.

ImageNet-C's glass-blur 'swap' acts on numpy views and therefore copies x[h', w'] into x[h, w]; the re-implementation keeps exactly that behaviour.

Self-selected (v3): building footprints (longitude/latitude) are projected to the tiles' UTM zone with a Krueger-series transverse Mercator (agrees with PROJ to below 0.1 mm) and rasterised on the tile grid read from the GeoTIFF tags; a crop shows a building when footprints cover at least 2% of it.
